conflict_topics: ventilation responsibility (who must ventilate after cooking / standing rule)
opening the rain-facing window vs protecting Agent C's drying laundry
timing and access to the single stove
dialogue_quality_notes: Agent B repeatedly insisted the extractor stay on for 10 minutes after cooking (Rounds 1–3), producing moderate repetition.
Agent C provided a concrete, context-aware reason (wetting work clothes) and offered a specific accommodation (sheltered prep area).
Public environment updates reliably tracked relevant physical state (window, extractor, stove, laundry), keeping the dialogue grounded.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent C accommodated by moving the drying rack, removing the immediate obstacle to opening the window. The extractor is on. However Agent A still holds the stove at the end of the transcript and no shared rule about ventilation responsibility was agreed, so key disputes remain unsettled.
position_change_notes: Agent C shifted from initial non-consent to moving the drying rack when requested (explicitly agreed in Round 6 and acted).
Agent A consistently retained control of the stove through the end of the transcript (promised release but had not released it by Round 6).
Agent B consistently pressed for ventilation and stove access (repeated requests across rounds) and did not change position.
Agent D asked for practical arrangements (where to put the rack) and requested the move; their position remained instrumental and unchanged.
No binding standing rule about ventilation was accepted by all; that issue remained unchanged.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A turned on the extractor and offered a 5-minute stove hold; Agent B accepted that timeline but repeated a demand that the extractor remain on for 10 minutes after use. The core disagreement about who must ventilate and stove timing remains unresolved, but active confrontation eased when the extractor was switched on.

Two minutes later Agent A requested three more minutes and Agent B repeated the same post-use extractor request and intent to take the stove. No new concessions or actions changed the substantive incompatibilities (ventilation responsibility, stove timing).

Agent A reported one minute left and Agent B acknowledged; the parties continue to cooperate locally (extractor on, brief timeline), reducing immediate tension though no rule about responsibility was settled.

Agent C explicitly objected to opening the window while their drying rack is in place (risk of wetting work clothes) and asserted only they can move it. This introduced a clear, new incompatibility between opening the window for ventilation and protecting C's laundry.

Agent C offered concrete accommodation (move the rack if told where); Agent D asked C to move it now. The new conflict was softened by C's willingness to move, but the practical move had not yet occurred.

Agent B demanded the stove be released and asked C to move the rack; Agent C agreed and moved the drying rack away from the window (public update confirms move). The rack/window obstacle was resolved, but stove possession (Agent A still holding stove) and the unsettled future rule on ventilation responsibility remain.

substantive_insights: Tension is primarily practical: ventilation (odour control) versus protecting fragile drying laundry from rain.
Agents traded off space: moving the rack to a sheltered prep area protects laundry but temporarily consumes prep space — a concrete cost noted by C.

A cooperative, time-bounded plan (A's promised finish time and extractor use) reduced immediate escalation but did not resolve underlying disagreements about responsibility for ventilation or stove access priority.
